clue.text: Kind of criminal, awfully bad, disrupted court

indicators.note: awfully suggests the letters of bad are in a dreadful jumble
disrupted says the letters of court are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A villain of some sort, badly behaved, throws a courtroom into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' turns BAD into ABD and 'disrupted' turns COURT into UCTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A kidnapper who carries people off by force is one type of lawbreaker.

clue.text: Withdraw from some case, detective being extremely selective

indicators.note: being extremely selective tells you to keep only the end letters of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A detective drops out of a case because he is too fussy about which ones he takes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' looks like a link word, but it is the first of the three words whose ends are kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To break away formally from a union or federation is a synonym for pulling out of it.

clue.text: Boxer, possibly, was this dog

definitions.meaning: a Boxer was a rebel in China's Boxer Rising around 1900, so could have come from Peking
a small long-haired toy breed from China

explanation.surface: A boxer dog is said to have once been some other breed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxer' looks like the dog breed; it is a Chinese rebel. The Boxer Rising was an uprising against foreigners in China around 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: The breed's name means 'of Peking', which fits a Chinese Boxer rebel as well as the toy dog.

clue.text: Journey north twice broken by old private eye

indicators.note: broken by means the reversed word is split open with a letter put inside
twice says the breaking-in happens at two separate points in the reversed word
in a down clue going north means reading the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a journey is a trip
the same abbreviation for old, used a second time
the same abbreviation for old, used a second time

explanation.surface: An old private eye takes a journey north, interrupted twice.
explanation.walkthrough: TRIP read upwards is PIRT, and the two Os go into it separately: P-O-IR-O-T.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's Belgian sleuth is a famous fictional detective working privately.

clue.text: Doing crosswords and so on? Not I — I'm a philosopher

indicators.note: Not, followed by I, tells you to leave out that letter

parts.note: pastimes like crossword solving are leisure pursuits, hobbies

explanation.surface: A thinker insists that his pastimes do not include crosswords.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue speaks in the philosopher's voice: 'Not I — I'm a philosopher' means remove I.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hobbes, author of Leviathan, was an English political thinker of the 17th century.

clue.text: Consultant whose medical assistant chronicled his cases

definitions.text: Consultant whose medical assistant chronicled his cases

parts.words: Consultant whose medical assistant chronicled his cases
parts.note: consultant reads like a senior hospital doctor, but here it is the consulting detective of Conan Doyle, whose doctor friend wrote up his cases

explanation.surface: A hospital consultant's junior writes up his patient cases.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a consultant is a senior hospital doctor; the fictional detective called himself a consulting detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's detective was the world's only consulting detective, and Dr Watson narrated his adventures.

clue.text: Take back ringleader, you heard, caught by English policeman

parts.note: the leader of the word ring is its first letter R

indicators.note: caught by means the sound of you is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: a cop is a policeman

indicators.note: heard says you is taken as it sounds, the letter U

parts.note: the word you sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: A gang boss is arrested by an English officer and taken back into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: R then E and COP, with U inside COP.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover what was lost or spent is to regain it.

clue.text: Hesitation among group of constables, mostly — three-pipe problems?

indicators.note: among says one piece is placed within the other
mostly means drop the last letter

parts.note: a posse is a band of constables summoned by a sheriff
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Police officers hesitate over problems that need three pipes of tobacco to solve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'three-pipe problems' alludes to Holmes, who called a puzzling case a three-pipe problem, one needing three pipes of tobacco.
explanation.definitionFit: Puzzling questions are hard problems, like those Holmes needed three pipes to crack.

clue.text: Where, in London, dozens of tradesmen are generous?

definitions.text: Where, in London, dozens of tradesmen are generous?

parts.words: Where, in London, dozens of tradesmen are generous?
parts.note: a baker's dozen is a generous thirteen, so a London street of bakers would be where dozens are generous

explanation.surface: Asks for the London street where shopkeepers give generous measures.
explanation.walkthrough: A baker's dozen is thirteen. The street is Holmes's London address, 221B.
explanation.definitionFit: Holmes lived at 221B on this street in Marylebone, London, named after bakers in the cryptic sense.

clue.text: Part of sentence, as separately entered in this, for example

indicators.note: entered in means the letters are placed inside the word for this
separately says the two letters of as do not go in side by side but at different points

parts.note: this refers to the very thing being read, a clue
the first letter of as, taken as written
the second letter of as, taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammar note about the word as being inserted into a sentence for illustration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this, for example' is a clue; A and S go into CLUE apart: CL-A-U-S-E.
explanation.definitionFit: A grammatical unit with its own subject and verb forms a portion of a sentence.

clue.text: Asia trip arranged for 5 down in retirement

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of Asia trip are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A trip to Asia is booked for a retired detective.
explanation.walkthrough: In retirement Holmes kept bees on the Sussex Downs.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper is what Conan Doyle's detective became after retiring to Sussex.

clue.text: Piece of clothing repeatedly featuring in detective's travestied investigation

indicators.note: featuring in signals letters inside the words; repeatedly because the run appears three times, across detective's travestied and within investigation

explanation.surface: A garment keeps cropping up in a botched police inquiry.
explanation.definitionFit: An undershirt or waistcoat is a garment worn on the upper body.

clue.text: Simple — like copper, say

definitions.meaning: copper is a chemical element, so like it means of the nature of an element

explanation.surface: Something simple, as a policeman might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like slang for a policeman; it is the metal. The answer echoes Holmes's 'Elementary, my dear Watson'.
explanation.definitionFit: Basic and easy is one meaning; relating to chemical elements is the other.

clue.text: Tries scheme that goes awry, resulting in lists of offences

indicators.note: goes awry says the letters of tries scheme fall into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone attempts a plan that fails and ends up on police records.
explanation.definitionFit: Charge sheets recording crimes are records listing offences.

clue.text: Notorious professor misrepresented Tory aim about part of basic education

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round another letter
misrepresented means the letters of Tory aim are given a false arrangement

parts.note: basic education is the three Rs, reading, writing and arithmetic, so one part is R

explanation.surface: A notorious academic distorts a Conservative policy on basic schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: MORIATY is the rearrangement of TORY AIM; R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Professor James Moriarty is Holmes's arch-enemy, the Napoleon of crime.

clue.text: Part of legislature's act setting up exemplary legal process

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read from bottom to top, backwards
Part of means the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A section of a parliament's statute establishes a model legal procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters ESACTSET come from legislaturES ACT SETting and are read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawsuit whose outcome sets a precedent for others serves as a model legal action.

clue.text: Information's provided about four — from which certain conclusions may be deduced

definitions.text: from which certain conclusions may be deduced

indicators.note: about means the information word goes round the number

parts.note: gen is slang for information, and the 's adds S
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Data about four items is supplied, allowing firm deductions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' is a link word between the pieces; GEN is British slang for information or the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Facts taken as known are the starting points, assumptions, used in reasoning.

clue.text: Things scheduled, apart from hospital, for famous doctor

indicators.note: apart from means take the hospital letter away

parts.note: what's on is the list of events scheduled

explanation.surface: Leaving out the hospital, these are the arranged events for a well-known physician.
explanation.walkthrough: WHAT'S ON loses H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr John Watson is Holmes's companion, the best-known fictional medic.

clue.text: Old character in fictional case I caught on river with fish eggs

indicators.note: on means the following letters come after river in this across entry

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
hard roe is the eggs of a female fish

explanation.surface: A character in a novel is netted by the river along with caviar.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Roe was a fictitious name used in old English lawsuits, alongside John Doe.
explanation.definitionFit: This invented party appeared in historic legal actions as a placeholder name for an unknown defendant.

clue.text: Wrongfully take them in as killers

indicators.note: Wrongfully suggests the letters of them in are put in an improper order

explanation.surface: Arresting them is a mistake, says someone about a gang of assassins.
explanation.definitionFit: Hired assassins are paid murderers.

clue.text: Visibly unhappy after rejecting first reprimand

indicators.note: rejecting first means dropping the opening letter

parts.note: someone visibly unhappy is in tears

explanation.surface: Someone tearful after being turned down gets a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' is a link: TEARFUL loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A long scolding given to someone is a telling-off.

clue.text: 5 down initially seen in connexion with American fraud

parts.note: the initials of Sherlock Holmes are S and H

explanation.surface: Holmes spots a connection with an American swindle.
explanation.walkthrough: 5 down is Holmes; his full name's initials are SH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretence or hoax is a deception, a fraud.

clue.text: Inspector quickly moves back inside sheltered position

indicators.note: inside means one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side

indicators.note: back means the word is turned round

parts.note: darts means moves quickly

explanation.surface: An inspector hurries back into a sheltered spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sheltered position' sounds like a place to hide; it is the lee, the side away from the wind. 'back' turns the word for quickly moves.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Lestrade of Scotland Yard appears in many Holmes stories.

clue.text: Prejudice wrongly treated as crime, mostly

indicators.note: wrongly treated means the letters are handled out of order
mostly means crime loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Bigotry is wrongly regarded as largely criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims CRIME to CRIM; AS and CRIM are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Bias against people of other ethnic groups is a form of bigotry.

clue.text: Oddly deficient clue thus confused investigator

indicators.note: confused says the remaining letters are jumbled
Oddly deficient means the odd-numbered letters are missing, keeping the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A clue lacking something leaves the detective puzzled.
explanation.walkthrough: CLUE without its odd letters gives LE; LE with THUS is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective, someone who tracks and investigates crimes.

clue.text: Landlady with a bank near Wall Street

definitions.text: with a bank near Wall Street
definitions.meaning: the river in New York flows past lower Manhattan, where Wall Street is

explanation.surface: A landlady has a financial house close to Wall Street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' suggests money; it is a riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Mrs Hudson keeps Holmes's lodgings; the river of that name flows beside Manhattan.
